clue.text: Bitter feeling of a colleague I'm interrupting

indicators.note: the contraction I'm breaks into the middle of the friend word, cutting it open

parts.note: a crony is a close companion or colleague
I'm contracted and written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone resents a co-worker who keeps butting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' puts IM inside CRONY, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is bitterness or ill feeling between people.

clue.text: Sculpture got broken

definitions.meaning: a carved head and shoulders on a plinth
past tense of the informal verb meaning to break, as in a smashed toy

explanation.definitionFit: A head-and-shoulders statue is one sense; the slangy past tense meaning smashed is the other.

clue.text: Spasmodic as not quite complete but suitable at first

indicators.note: this word is to be placed at the start, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: fit means suitable or appropriate

indicators.note: not quite means the word for complete loses its final letter

parts.note: full means complete or entire

explanation.surface: A sentence about something judged only partly finished yet fine at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last L of FULL, giving FUL; 'at first' puts FIT before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fitful comes in irregular bursts, which is what spasmodic describes.

clue.text: Guide to go slowly over sultanate

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: to drag is to move or pass slowly
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: Advice to a tour guide to dawdle while crossing an Arabian country.
explanation.walkthrough: A dragoman is an interpreter and guide in Arabic-speaking lands, which fits the Omani surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman is an interpreter and guide for travellers in the Middle East.

clue.text: Being alfresco makes a difference to our foods

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are changed, made different in their order

explanation.surface: Eating outside alters the taste of what we eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a difference' rearranges TO OUR FOODS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco means in the open air, outside the house.

clue.text: Where leaders of country lie ill, nursed in comfort?

definitions.text: Where leaders of country lie ill, nursed in comfort?

indicators.note: the leaders of each word are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: Presidents and kings convalesce in luxury somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the last six words spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes a place where the sick are cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical centre is where ill people are looked after by staff.

clue.text: Inform in a whimsical speech

indicators.note: speech signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: quaint means whimsical or oddly old-fashioned, preceded by A

explanation.surface: Someone delivers news in a fanciful address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A quaint' spoken sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone aware of facts is to tell or familiarise them.

clue.text: Play idly with one's food

definitions.meaning: to toy or fiddle with something without seriousness
a layered dessert of sponge, custard and cream

explanation.surface: A child pushing dinner round the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: A TRIFLE is a classic British pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something carelessly, and a layered custard dessert.

clue.text: Foreign money is a nuisance-no head on it

indicators.note: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: trouble is a nuisance or bother

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that currency abroad is a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no head on it' removes the first letter T of TROUBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency unit of Russia.

clue.text: Sediment is disturbed by lieutenant

indicators.note: the second piece stands beside the first
disturbed means the two letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An officer stirs up the mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns IS into SI, then LT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt is fine sand and mud deposited by water.

clue.text: Reasonable excuse to go to place of entertainment

parts.note: fair means reasonable or just
a ground is a reason or justification, an excuse

explanation.surface: A fair pretext for an outing to a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A site where rides, stalls and sideshows are set up for fun.

clue.text: Mark book-it's the truth

definitions.meaning: one of the four New Testament accounts of Jesus is attributed to Mark
something completely true, as in an unquestioned statement

explanation.surface: A teacher grading a book insists their assessment is accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a verb meaning grade; it is the evangelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament account by Mark is one; absolute truth is the other.

clue.text: This is never a quick examination

definitions.text: This is never a quick examination

parts.words: This is never a quick examination
parts.note: quick in its old sense means living, so this inspection is always of the dead, never of the living

explanation.surface: A complaint that some inspection always drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The quick and the dead' uses quick to mean alive.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy is a medical inspection of a corpse after death.

clue.text: Ineffective person makes fortune, crossing a sea

indicators.note: the fortune word straddles the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: luck means fortune or chance
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A hapless person strikes it rich on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts A MED inside LUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is someone weak or unsuccessful who needs help.

clue.text: He's always agreeable to have as a companion

definitions.text: He's always agreeable to have as a companion

parts.words: He's always agreeable to have as a companion
parts.note: a person who never disagrees seems pleasant company, but the phrase points at a sycophant who assents to everything

explanation.surface: Praise for an easy-going friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who agrees with whatever a superior says.

clue.text: Pay off debt-more, as it turns out

indicators.note: turns out signals the letters being turned into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone discovers they owe more than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges MORE AS IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise is to reduce a loan gradually through regular payments.

clue.text: Bury Ben and Tom-they fell together

indicators.note: the two names collapse into a jumbled heap of letters

explanation.surface: Two men toppled at the same moment and must be laid to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell together' mixes BEN and TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a body in a tomb is to inter it.

clue.text: As magistrate, order wine container with port

indicators.note: the second piece comes with, alongside, the first

parts.note: a bin is a rack or store for wine bottles
Dover is an English Channel port

explanation.surface: A JP calls for a wine rack and some port.
explanation.walkthrough: In British law, a magistrate can bind someone over to keep the peace; DOVER is a ferry port in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind over is a court requirement that someone behave or appear later.

clue.text: Go for old record in quick run

indicators.note: the record sits in the middle of the run

parts.note: a dart is a sudden quick dash
an EP is an extended-play record, an older format

explanation.surface: Someone nips out for a vintage disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts EP inside DART.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave or set off.

clue.text: Early flower quietly came up beyond the boundary

indicators.note: the rising word sits after, beyond, the edge word

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
a rim is an edge or border
rose means came up or ascended

explanation.surface: A bloom pokes up silently past the edge of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow bloom that appears in spring.

clue.text: Show engineers some meat

parts.note: the RE are the Royal Engineers of the British Army
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: Army sappers display a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose or make visible.

clue.text: Chip shop where they rake it in? You bet!

definitions.text: Chip shop where they rake it in? You bet!

parts.words: Chip shop where they rake it in? You bet!
parts.note: the chips are gaming tokens, not fried potatoes, and the croupier rakes them across the table where punters wager

explanation.surface: A thriving fish-and-chip shop making big profits.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'chip shop' in Britain sells fried fish and chips; here the chips are gambling tokens.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house where people stake money on games of chance.

clue.text: Openly confessing-and arrested by police

indicators.note: the police abbreviation holds the joining word inside it, like a suspect in custody

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A suspect owns up after being taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrested by' puts AND inside CID.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and honest in speech.

clue.text: Tax too much for bowling coach

parts.note: in cricket the bowling is delivered in overs of six balls
to train is to coach

explanation.surface: A cricket coach working the bowlers too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER in cricket is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax is to strain, so this means push beyond safe limits.

clue.text: Produce handle of whip

definitions.meaning: the short stock of a riding whip

explanation.definitionFit: A harvest of grain is one sense; the stock of a rider's whip is the other.

clue.text: Quote from a particular place out loud

indicators.note: out loud means the word is heard spoken, not read

parts.note: a site is a particular location

explanation.surface: Someone reads a passage from a named location.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to refer to or mention a source as evidence.

clue.text: Press for evidence of identity

definitions.meaning: documents such as a passport carried to prove who one is

explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers are one sense; identity documents are the other.

clue.text: Round about ten, their unlucky number

indicators.note: round about signals the letters being spun around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a figure near ten that a group finds ill-omened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round about' rearranges TEN THEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is the number superstitiously held to bring bad luck.
